definitions.explanation: a household where both partners are employed and contribute to the family income

examples.japanese: {共働|ともばたら}きの{夫婦|ふうふ}が{増|ふ}えている。
examples.english: The number of dual-income couples is increasing.

examples.japanese: {共働|ともばたら}きだと{家事|かじ}の{分担|ぶんたん}が{大切|たいせつ}だ。
examples.english: When both work, sharing housework is important.

examples.japanese: {共働|ともばたら}きでも{子育|こそだ}てと{両立|りょうりつ}している。
examples.english: Even with both working, they balance work and child-rearing.

notes:
SOCIAL VOCABULARY:
{共働|ともばたら}き describes households where both partners work outside the home.

CULTURAL NOTE:
{共働|ともばたら}き has become increasingly common in Japan as:
- Women's labor force participation has increased
- Economic necessity requires dual incomes
- Attitudes toward gender roles have shifted

CHALLENGES:
- {家事|かじ}{分担|ぶんたん} - division of housework
- {育児|いくじ}と{仕事|しごと}の{両立|りょうりつ} - balancing childcare and work
- {待機|たいき}{児童|じどう} - daycare waiting lists

RELATED WORDS:
- {専業|せんぎょう}{主婦|しゅふ} - full-time homemaker
- {兼業|けんぎょう} - holding multiple jobs
- ワンオペ{育児|いくじ} - single-parent-style childcare (when one parent does all)
- {家事|かじ}{育児|いくじ} - housework and childcare

OTHER READING:
Also pronounced as ともかせぎ, though ともばたらき is more common.
